rows.stem: In the electrolysis of water, the mass ratio of hydrogen and oxygen gases liberated at the electrodes is :
rows.solution:
Electrolysis of water gives hydrogen and oxygen in the volume ratio 2 : 1:

\(\mathrm{2H_2O(l) \xrightarrow{\text{electric current}} 2H_2(g) + O_2(g)}\)

By mass, 2 moles of \(\mathrm{H_2}\) weigh \(2 \times 2 = 4\) g and 1 mole of \(\mathrm{O_2}\) weighs 32 g, so the mass ratio of hydrogen to oxygen is \(4 : 32 = 1 : 8\).

This is option (C) 1 : 8.

rows.stem: Select the correct option from the following statements about the functioning of the human heart.

options.label: A
options.text: Right atrium receives deoxygenated blood from different parts of the body and sends it to pulmonary veins.

options.label: B
options.text: Left atrium sends oxygenated blood to right ventricle which pumps it to different parts of the body.

options.label: C
options.text: Right atrium receives deoxygenated blood from the body and sends it to the right ventricle.

options.label: D
options.text: Left atrium receives oxygenated blood from the pulmonary arteries and sends it to the left ventricle.

rows.solution:
The right atrium receives deoxygenated blood from different parts of the body (through the vena cava) and passes it to the right ventricle, which pumps it to the lungs. The other statements are wrong: the right atrium does not send blood to the pulmonary veins, the left atrium sends blood to the left ventricle (not the right), and the left atrium receives oxygenated blood from the pulmonary veins, not the pulmonary arteries.

This is option (C) Right atrium receives deoxygenated blood from the body and sends it to the right ventricle.

rows.stem: Which of the following is the correct sequence of parts of female reproductive system of flowering plants in terms of their placement ?

options.label: A
options.text: Stigma, ovule, ovary, style

options.label: B
options.text: Ovule, stigma, ovary, style

options.label: C
options.text: Style, stigma, ovule, ovary

options.label: D
options.text: Stigma, style, ovary, ovule

rows.solution:
The female reproductive part of a flower, the pistil, has a sticky stigma at the top, a long style below it, and the swollen ovary at the base; the ovules lie inside the ovary. So in order of placement the parts are stigma, style, ovary, ovule.

This is option (D) Stigma, style, ovary, ovule.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem: The part of the human eye which can modify the curvature of the eye lens to some extent is :

options.label: A
options.text: Pupil

options.label: B
options.text: Cornea

options.label: C
options.text: Ciliary muscles

options.label: D
options.text: Aqueous humour

rows.solution:
The curvature of the eye lens is changed to some extent by the ciliary muscles: when they relax the lens becomes thin, and when they contract the lens becomes thicker. This is how the eye adjusts its focal length (accommodation).

This is option (C) Ciliary muscles.

rows.subtopic: Physical Properties of Metals and Non-metals
rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Ductility is that property of metals which enables copper to be used in making cooking utensils.

**Reason (R) :** Copper is a metal which is ductile as well as malleable.
rows.context: For Questions number 17 to 20, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is **not** the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
Copper is used for cooking utensils because it is a good conductor of heat (and is malleable enough to be shaped). Ductility is the property of being drawn into wires, which is why copper is used for electric wires, not utensils. So the Assertion is false.

Copper is indeed both ductile and malleable, so the Reason is true.

This is option (D) Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** The bending of a wire in the form of a coil of several turns does not affect its electrical resistance.

**Reason (R) :** The electrical resistance of a wire is directly proportional to its electrical resistivity.
rows.context: For Questions number 17 to 20, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is **not** the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
The resistance of a wire is \(R = \rho \dfrac{l}{A}\). Bending a wire into a coil of several turns changes neither its material, nor its length, nor its area of cross-section, so its resistance is unchanged. The Assertion is true.

The Reason says that the resistance of a wire is directly proportional to its resistivity. For a wire of given length and area of cross-section, \(R = \rho \dfrac{l}{A}\) does make \(R\) directly proportional to \(\rho\), so read in the usual way the Reason is true. It does not explain the Assertion, which rests on the length and area staying the same. On that reading the answer would be that both statements are true and the Reason is not the correct explanation.

The marking scheme treats the Reason as false, presumably because the resistance of a wire depends on its length and area of cross-section as well as on its resistivity, so it is not fixed by the resistivity alone.

The marking scheme's answer is option (C) Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

rows.stem: What are micelles ? Draw the structure.
rows.solution:
A micelle is a cluster of soap molecules formed in water. A soap molecule has a long hydrocarbon tail, which is hydrophobic (soluble in oil, insoluble in water), and an ionic end, which is hydrophilic (soluble in water). In water the molecules arrange themselves with the hydrophobic tails in the interior of the cluster, towards the oil or dirt, and the ionic ends on the surface of the cluster, facing the water. Such a cluster is called a micelle.

Structure: draw an oil droplet at the centre with many soap molecules arranged radially around it, each drawn as a wavy line (the hydrocarbon tail) pointing into the oil droplet and ending in a small circle (the ionic head, \(\mathrm{{-}COO^-}\)) on the outside, with \(\mathrm{Na^+}\) ions shown around the outer surface. Label the oil droplet, the hydrocarbon tails and the ionic ends.

rows.subtopic: Human Brain and Protection of Nervous Tissue
rows.stem: A person is making a list to purchase few things from a nearby market. Explain how the fore-brain plays an important role in performing this activity.
rows.solution:
The fore-brain is the main thinking part of the brain. It receives sensory impulses and also controls voluntary actions. In making a shopping list:

Thinking and memory: the fore-brain thinks about and recalls what is needed at home and decides what to buy.

Voluntary action: it sends messages to the muscles of the hand to write the list.

Sensory areas: its areas for sight (and hearing) let the person read the list and take in information, for example from someone at home.

rows.stem: How and why is an electric fuse used in an electric circuit ? Briefly describe its function.
rows.solution:
An electric fuse is a safety device connected in series with the device or circuit it protects.

It is used to prevent damage to the circuit and the appliance from an unduly high electric current. The fuse wire is made of a material with a low melting point. If a current larger than the specified value flows through the circuit (because of overloading or a short circuit), the heat produced melts the fuse wire, which breaks the circuit and stops the current.

rows.stem:
Two substances ‘A’ and ‘B’ are burnt in air separately. For ‘A’, ashes are collected and dissolved in water to get solution ‘X’, while for ‘B’, fumes produced are passed through water to get solution ‘Y’. Both the solutions ‘X’ and ‘Y’ are then tested with pH paper.

(a) If ‘X’ gives light blue colour and ‘Y’ gives orange colour to the pH paper, then write the nature and range of pH of ‘X’ and ‘Y’.

(b) Which one of the two – A and B, is a metal ? Justify your answer.
rows.solution:
(a) Light blue on pH paper shows that X is basic, with a pH of about 9 to 11. Orange shows that Y is acidic, with a pH of about 4 to 6.

(b) A is the metal. Metals burn in air to form metal oxides, which are basic, so the solution of the ashes of A is basic. Non-metals form acidic oxides, which is why the fumes of B dissolve in water to give the acidic solution Y.

rows.stem:
A pure pea plant bearing terminal flowers was cross-pollinated with a pure plant having axillary flowers. In \(\mathrm{F_1}\) generation, plants with axial flowers only were obtained. \(\mathrm{F_1}\) generation plants are self-pollinated and \(\mathrm{F_2}\) generation is obtained.

(a) Work out the pattern of inheritance in this case.

(b) What will be the ratio of plants obtained in \(\mathrm{F_2}\) generation ?
rows.solution:
(a) Axillary position of flowers is dominant (all \(\mathrm{F_1}\) plants have axillary flowers) and terminal position is recessive. Let A stand for axillary and a for terminal.

Parents: pure axillary AA and pure terminal aa. Gametes: A and a.

\(\mathrm{F_1}\) generation: all Aa, all with axillary flowers.

\(\mathrm{F_2}\) generation (Aa \(\times\) Aa): each parent gives gametes A and a, and the crosses give

AA (axillary), Aa (axillary), Aa (axillary), aa (terminal).

(b) In the \(\mathrm{F_2}\) generation the ratio is 3 axillary : 1 terminal (3 : 1). The genotype ratio is AA : Aa : aa = 1 : 2 : 1.

rows.stem: A convex mirror used for rear view on an automobile has a focal length of \(1{\cdot}5\) m. If a 3 m high bus is located at \(6{\cdot}0\) m from the mirror, use mirror formula to determine the position and size of the image of the bus as seen in the mirror.
rows.solution:
For a convex mirror the focal length is positive: \(f = +1{\cdot}5\) m. The bus is in front of the mirror: \(u = -6{\cdot}0\) m, and its height \(h = 3\) m.

By the mirror formula, \(\dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}\):

\(\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{f} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{1{\cdot}5} + \dfrac{1}{6} = \dfrac{4}{6} + \dfrac{1}{6} = \dfrac{5}{6}\)

so \(v = \dfrac{6}{5} = +1{\cdot}2\) m. The image is 1.2 m behind the mirror.

Size of the image: \(m = \dfrac{h'}{h} = -\dfrac{v}{u} = -\dfrac{1{\cdot}2}{-6{\cdot}0} = +0{\cdot}2\), so \(h' = 0{\cdot}2 \times 3 = 0{\cdot}6\) m.

The image is virtual, erect and diminished, 0.6 m high.

rows.stem: Some harmful chemicals get accumulated in human bodies through the food chain. Name this phenomenon. Explain the reason of maximum concentration of these chemicals found in our bodies.
rows.solution:
The phenomenon is biological magnification.

Harmful chemicals such as pesticides are not biodegradable. They are taken up from the soil and water by plants and pass along the food chain, accumulating progressively at each trophic level. Human beings occupy the top level in many food chains, so the maximum concentration of these chemicals accumulates in our bodies.
